sections.html: Hypsophrys nicaraguensis is one of the most unusual cichlids in Central America in terms of behavior and one of the most beautiful in terms of coloration. Males grow to a maximum length of 25 cm, females are usually only 10-12 cm (maximum 18 cm).
Only captive-bred specimens are available in stores.

The Nicaragua cichlid is found not only in Nicaragua but also in Costa Rica. The Costa Rican variant, recognizable by the blue head of both sexes, is much more common in the hobby. Animals from Nicaragua have a copper-red head.
Despite its maximum size, the animals should be provided with aquariums that are as large as possible, in which they can grow into magnificent specimens.

The chemical composition of the water is irrelevant, but it should not be very soft or acidic. The temperature can range between 22 and 28°C, and it does not matter if it is slightly lower or higher at times.
They eat all standard ornamental fish food.
H. nicaraguensis has been a popular aquarium fish since the 1970s, as it is considered to be exceptionally peaceful for a cichlid.

The females usually have a longitudinal stripe and no pattern on their fins, while the males usually have a diamond-shaped spot on their flank and clearly patterned fins. Males are significantly larger than females. Sexual maturity is reached at lengths of around 12 cm (males) and 9 cm (females).

Unlike other "Cichlasoma" cichlids, which are open breeders attaching their eggs to a stone, a root or an aquarium pane, the eggs of the Nicaragua cichlid do not stick; they are freely movable, like mouthbrooder's eggs. This is why H. nicaraguensis prefers to spawn in shelters (caves or sand pits) where the spawn is not easily swept away. The females in a clutch initially grow faster than their brothers, but the males more than catch up later on.
